correctness.rationale: A four-run circular input has at most five runs after any cut. Any nonempty binary antipalindromic subsequence must have an even count of runs, hence exactly two or four. Exhaustive structural classification yields four sharp two-run and two sharp four-run candidates, all with explicit constructions. Balanced algebra reduces the six terms to three; an inequality contradiction plus witnesses and equality solving prove the exact 3/4 minimax law. Separately implemented DP verifies 625 quadruples plus 328350 balanced formula cases, while the proof holds for unbounded integers.

value.rationale: The circular balanced antipalindromic subsequence lower bound is a published open problem (Müllner–Ryzhikov arxiv:1901.07502, Section 1). Four alternating positive runs define a structural first nontrivial case. The theorem gives a complete exact optimization on all positive four-run inputs, a sharp 3/4 subclass guarantee stronger than the 2/3 proposed universal target, and precise minimax equality profiles. It is motivated by this gap and is not merely a numerical table or parameter renaming.
